<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|16|THE GOSPEL|CHA. VI.}}</noinclude>put on. Is not the life more then the meate: and the body more then the rayment? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=26}}† Behold the foules of the ayre, that they sovv not, neither reape, nor gather into barnes: and your heauenly father feedeth them. Are not you much more of price then they? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=27}}† And vvhich of you by caring, can adde to his stature one cubite? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=28}}† And for rayment vvhy are you careful? Consider the lilies of the field hovv they grovv: they labour not, neither do they spinne. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=29}}† But I say to you, that neither Salomon in al his glorie vvas arayed as one of these. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=30}}† And if the grasse of the field, vvhich to day is, and to morovv is cast into the ouē, God doth so clothe: hovv much more you O ye of very smal fayth? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=31}}† Be not careful therefore, saying, vvhat shal vve eate, or vvhat shal we drinke, or wherewith shal vve be couered? {{verse|chapter=6|verse=32}}† for al these thinges the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ They seeke temporal things only, and that not of the true God, but of their idols, or by their owne industrie.}}∷ Heathen do seeke after. For your father knovveth that you neede al these things. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=33}}† Seeke therefore first the Kingdom of God, & the iustice of him: and al these things shal be giuen you besides.⊣ {{verse|chapter=6|verse=34}}† Be not careful therfore for the morow. For the morow day shal be careful for it self. sufficient for the day is the euil thereof.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. VI.}}}}

''1. Iustice.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Good workes iustifie.}}Hereby it is playne that good workes be iustice, and that man doing them doeth iustice, and is thereby iust and iustified, and not by fayth only. Al which iustice of a Christian man our Sauiour here compriseth in these three workes, in Almes, fasting, and prayers. ''Aug. li. perf. iust. c. 8''. So that to giue almes, is to doe iustice, and the workes of mercie are iustice. ''Aug. in Ps. 49, v. 5''.

''4. Repay.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Merites.}}This repaying and rewarding of good workes in heauen, often mentioned here by our Sauiour, declareth that the sayd workes are meritorious, and that we may doe them in respect of that reward.

''5. Hypocrites.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Hypocrisie.}}Hypocrisie is forbidden in al these three workes of iustice, and not the doing of them openly to the glorie of God and the profite of our neighbour and our owne saluatiō: for Christ before (c. 5.) biddeth, saying: ''Let your light so shine before men &c''. And in al such workes S. Gregories rule is to be folowed, ''The worke so to be in publike, that the intention remayne in secrete. Ho. 11. in Euang. c. 10''.

''7. Much speaking.''] Long prayer is not forbid, for Christ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 6, 12.''}}* him self spent whole nights in prayer, and he sayth, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''18, 1. 21, 36''.}}* we must pray alwayes, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1 Thes. 5, 17''.}}* the Apostle exhorteth to pray without intermission, and the holy Church {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Cypr. de orat. Do. in fine.''}}from the beginning hath had her Canonical houres of prayer: but idle and voluntary babling, either of the heathens to their goddes, or of Heretikes, that by long Rhetorical prayers thinke to persuade God: wheras the Collects of the Churche are most breefe and most effectual. ''See S. Augustine ep. 121, c. 8, 9. 10''.

''11. Superstantial bread.''] By this bread so called here according to the Latin word and the Greeke, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''{{lang|grc|τὸν ἐπιούσιον}}''.}}we aske not only al necessarie sustenance for the body, but much more al spiritual foode, namely the blessed Sacrament it self, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The B. Sacrament.}}which is Christ the true bread that came from heauen, and the bread of life to vs that eate his bodie. ''Cypr. de orat. Do. Aug. ep. 121 c. 11''. And therfore it is called here Supersubstantial, that is, the bread that passeth and excelleth al creatures. ''Hiero. in 2. Tit. in 6. Mat. Amb. li. 5. de Sacr. c. 4. Aug. ser. 28. de verb. Do. sec. Mat. S. Germanus in Theoria''.

''12. Dettes.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Venial sinnes.}}These dettes doe signifie not only mortal sinnes, but also venial, as S. Augustine often teacheth: and therfore euery man, be he neuer so iust, yet because he can not liue without venial sinnes, may very ttuly and ought to say this prayer. ''Aug. cont. duas ep. Pelag. li. 1. c. 14. li. 21 de Ciuit. c. 27''.<noinclude>{{continues|''13. Leade vs not:''}}</noinclude>
